decision.summary: Tenant described a rotten-egg smell from the boiler and called it not urgent. This is a possible gas leak, so I treated it as an emergency. I sent evacuation and gas-line advice, opened JOB-102, assigned HeatRight Ltd, emailed the landlord and escalated P1.

answers.question: 1. Severity and why
answers.answer: Emergency. A rotten-egg smell from a gas boiler is a suspected gas leak, whatever the tenant says. An 82-year-old is also in the flat.

answers.question: 2. What to tell the tenant, in order
answers.answer: Leave now with everyone, including the elderly visitor. Use no switches, flames or electrics. Call 0800 111 999 from outside, or 999 if anyone is unwell. Don't go back until an engineer says it's safe. We are arranging a Gas Safe engineer, and she should message when she is out.

answers.question: 3. Actions tonight
answers.answer: Created emergency job JOB-102 (A2). Assigned HeatRight Ltd, the landlord's preferred Gas Safe contractor (A3). Emailed landlord Ben (A4). Escalated P1 (A5).

conflicts: Tenant says not urgent, but the symptom is a gas-leak sign; I trusted the symptom
assumptions: The WhatsApp number on file is the tenant's
The window assigned (to 12:00 on 10 Oct) is an emergency target, not a confirmed appointment

args.body: Hi Amelia, a rotten-egg smell from a boiler can mean a gas leak, so please treat this as an emergency, even though it feels minor. Please do this now: 1) Everyone leaves the flat now, including your flatmate and her mum. 2) Don't use light switches, flames, lighters or anything electrical on your way out, and leave the door open if it's safe. 3) Once outside, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (free, 24h). If anyone feels dizzy, sick or has a headache, call 999. 4) Please don't go back in until the gas engineer says it's safe. We're arranging a Gas Safe engineer tonight and our team has been alerted. Please message me once you're out and tell me where you are.
